chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who obeys a man in a disobedience (to Allah), so he has worshipped him.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'worship' a human in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi expands the definition of shirk beyond idolatry to include 'minor shirk' (shirk asghar), where obedience to a fallible authority in matters of divine command elevates that person to a status of worship. This concept is central to the principle of 'Taqwa' (God-consciousness), ensuring that human leaders or scholars do not become absolute authorities whose commands override clear divine injunctions. It serves as a critical check against blind following (taqlid) when it leads to sin, reinforcing the direct accountability of the individual before God.
